Research done 2026-08-04, findings reported in chat (not yet a docs/ file or implemented).

Platform facts (verified against primary sources):
- LinkedIn: old custom URLs do NOT redirect; stay linked 6 months (7 days if unlinked) then anyone can claim them, so a stored slug can become a stranger's profile. API is self-only (no third-party lookup), scraping is ToS-banned -> LinkedIn cannot be monitored, only detect-and-flag.
- X: closed free/Basic/Pro tiers to new devs Feb 2026; pay-per-use ~$0.005-0.01 per read. Username -> stable numeric id via GET /2/users/by/username (Composio TWITTER_USER_LOOKUP_BY_USERNAME wraps it; execute test was permission-denied in session, unverified end to end). OFFICIAL id-based link: x.com/intent/user?user_id=<id> - X docs themselves say "A screen_name may change; we recommend using user_id whenever possible". x.com/i/user/<id> also resolves but is undocumented; both are JS-shell pages, curl cannot verify the client-side redirect.
- Instagram: numeric pk is stable across renames. VERIFIED 2026-08-04: i.instagram.com/api/v1/users/web_profile_info/?username=X with x-ig-app-id 936619743392459 returns the pk unauthenticated from a residential IP (got 25025320 for @instagram). Will likely be blocked from datacenter IPs -> resolve on-device, not from Convex. Deep link instagram://user?id=<pk> opens by id in the app.
- LinkedIn: VERIFIED unauthenticated profile fetch returns status 999 (bot wall) -> even detect-and-flag cannot run server-side; staleness must be age-based + user-confirmed.
- Apple: no API anywhere resolves an arbitrary phone number to a person; only the user's own address book on device. Haven's deployment target is iOS 17.0, so best way = CNContactPickerViewController (zero permission, works on 17) + ContactAccessButton enhancement under #available(iOS 18) (queryString search over unshared contacts, per-contact grant, ignoredEmails/ignoredPhoneNumbers params). PhoneNumberKit 5.x is already a project dependency for E.164.

Codebase gaps found (see people.ts):
- addPerson and editPerson do NO handle dedup; only saveSharedProfile checks personHandles by_user_and_platform_and_valueKey (.unique() can throw once web created dup owners, jamming the iOS capture queue).
- No merge mutation exists server-side; graph/ has the merge model to port (MergeCandidate, merged|separate, keyed on normalized identifiers).
- people.contactHandles has no verified/provenance field (only profiles.handles does, and only X sets it).
- Three disagreeing phone normalizers (ContactValue PhoneNumberKit device-region, graph hardcoded +1, reach.ts as-typed) -> same phone can make two valueKeys.
- A re-share under a renamed username misses the valueKey index and creates a second person.

Composio state (corrected 2026-08-05): PR #212 merged convex/composio.ts - Composio owns OWN-card handle collection (LinkedIn vanityName+photo proven live, Instagram creator/business only with OAuthException 190 for personal, X TWITTER_USER_LOOKUP_ME wired but NOT live-proven). Clerk still owns sign-in. The same profile tools also return stable platform ids (LinkedIn member id, IG user_id, X id) - free platformId capture at connect time, not yet stored.

2026-08-05 additions:
- iOS 18 supports the exact same devices as iOS 17 (A12/XS+), so bumping Haven's 17.0 target to 18 excludes only non-updaters; recommended.
- Contacts change-history API (token diff at app open) detects newly added contacts; no true background contacts trigger exists on iOS.
- Contacts app shares are vCards; HavenShare can accept public.vcard and parse names/numbers with no permission.
- LinkedIn Connections.csv export includes a URL column for 1st-degree connections - the legitimate slug-refresh channel ("the follow survives the rename", serialized).
- WhatsApp identity = phone number; wa.me never rots; Composio WhatsApp toolkit is Business-API send-only, cannot read personal accounts.
- Scraping vendors (monid.ai = gateway over Apify/Browserbase etc.) rejected for LinkedIn v1: ToS enforcement (Proxycurl precedent), privacy posture of shipping saved people's names to a broker, and nothing to diff once the slug is dead.
- Flow diagrams artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/d199bb99-687f-4802-b365-177466c755ea

Key fixes: editPerson carries forward source/platformId/addedAt on unchanged (platform,valueKey); X id resolved PRE-save via new composio:resolveXUsername (post-save patch was wrong sequencing - rename dedup never fired); mergeHandleIntoOwner refuses rename onto a valueKey another person owns; addPerson back to bare-id return (old tabs safe), outcomes live on addPersonWithOutcome; digitless phone values rejected (were colliding strangers via lowercase fallback); capture attach fills empty headline/bio/link/screenshotId; web suggester pool = new listPersonNames query (Convex text search cannot typo-match); owner tiebreak by person _creationTime not row age; appendContext idempotent (replay-safe); shared 50/day cap on X lookups; logs redacted. iOS: picker uses delegate-provided CNContact (store refetch dead under denied); suggestions gated to full access only; handle_taken inline UX. content.text:
Round 2 is complete. All six correctness defects and all three standards items are fixed, and this time every fix is verified at the call-site level, not by report.

## What round 2 fixed

- **The unwired fix (defect 1)** - the serious one. The digitless-phone gate existed only as a helper with a unit test; nothing called it. It's now wired into all five places the original spec named: server validation (covering `addPerson`, `editPerson`, `saveSharedProfile`), profile handles, both capture paths, and the web client. The proof is the reviewer's own scenario as a regression test - the sidekick reverted the fix with `git stash`, watched the test fail with Bob merged into Alice, restored it, and watched it pass.
- **`editPerson` rename guard** - the ID-first lookup now also asks who owns the *new* username, refusing with `handle_taken` instead of double-indexing.
- **Equal-value ID enrichment** - a re-share that carries a freshly resolved ID now enriches the stored handle, so the full chain (save without ID, re-share with ID, later rename) attaches to the same person end to end. This was the missing link that could still mint twins after a rename.
- **Note replay detection** matches whole notes, not substrings - "Acme" no longer counts as a replay of "Met at Acme".
- **Capture conflicts** return a real status and keep the capture in triage instead of minting a third corrupt identity; the test that asserted the corruption as expected now asserts the refusal. description: "2026-08-04 research on the three leads - Apple contact lookup by phone, attach-vs-create for multi-platform profiles, and social URL rot (LinkedIn unmonitorable, X /i/user/id permalink, IG pk)"

Research done 2026-08-04, findings reported in chat (not yet a docs/ file or implemented).

Platform facts (verified against primary sources):
- LinkedIn: old custom URLs do NOT redirect; stay linked 6 months (7 days if unlinked) then anyone can claim them, so a stored slug can become a stranger's profile. API is self-only (no third-party lookup), scraping is ToS-banned -> LinkedIn cannot be monitored, only detect-and-flag.
- X: closed free/Basic/Pro tiers to new devs Feb 2026; pay-per-use ~$0.005-0.01 per read. Username -> stable numeric id via GET /2/users/by/username (Composio TWITTER_USER_LOOKUP_BY_USERNAME wraps it; execute test was permission-denied in session, unverified end to end). OFFICIAL id-based link: x.com/intent/user?user_id=<id> - X docs themselves say "A screen_name may change; we recommend using user_id whenever possible". x.com/i/user/<id> also resolves but is undocumented; both are JS-shell pages, curl cannot verify the client-side redirect.
- Instagram: numeric pk is stable across renames. VERIFIED 2026-08-04: i.instagram.com/api/v1/users/web_profile_info/?username=X with x-ig-app-id 936619743392459 returns the pk unauthenticated from a residential IP (got 25025320 for @instagram). Will likely be blocked from datacenter IPs -> resolve on-device, not from Convex. Deep link instagram://user?id=<pk> opens by id in the app.
- LinkedIn: VERIFIED unauthenticated profile fetch returns status 999 (bot wall) -> even detect-and-flag cannot run server-side; staleness must be age-based + user-confirmed.
- Apple: no API anywhere resolves an arbitrary phone number to a person; only the user's own address book on device. Haven's deployment target is iOS 17.0, so best way = CNContactPickerViewController (zero permission, works on 17) + ContactAccessButton enhancement under #available(iOS 18) (queryString search over unshared contacts, per-contact grant, ignoredEmails/ignoredPhoneNumbers params). PhoneNumberKit 5.x is already a project dependency for E.164.

Codebase gaps found (see people.ts):
- addPerson and editPerson do NO handle dedup; only saveSharedProfile checks personHandles by_user_and_platform_and_valueKey (.unique() can throw once web created dup owners, jamming the iOS capture queue).
- No merge mutation exists server-side; graph/ has the merge model to port (MergeCandidate, merged|separate, keyed on normalized identifiers).
- people.contactHandles has no verified/provenance field (only profiles.handles does, and only X sets it).
- Three disagreeing phone normalizers (ContactValue PhoneNumberKit device-region, graph hardcoded +1, reach.ts as-typed) -> same phone can make two valueKeys.
- A re-share under a renamed username misses the valueKey index and creates a second person.

Composio state (corrected 2026-08-05): PR #212 merged convex/composio.ts - Composio owns OWN-card handle collection (LinkedIn vanityName+photo proven live, Instagram creator/business only with OAuthException 190 for personal, X TWITTER_USER_LOOKUP_ME wired but NOT live-proven). Clerk still owns sign-in. The same profile tools also return stable platform ids (LinkedIn member id, IG user_id, X id) - free platformId capture at connect time, not yet stored.

2026-08-05 additions:
- iOS 18 supports the exact same devices as iOS 17 (A12/XS+), so bumping Haven's 17.0 target to 18 excludes only non-updaters; recommended.
- Contacts change-history API (token diff at app open) detects newly added contacts; no true background contacts trigger exists on iOS.
- Contacts app shares are vCards; HavenShare can accept public.vcard and parse names/numbers with no permission.
- LinkedIn Connections.csv export includes a URL column for 1st-degree connections - the legitimate slug-refresh channel ("the follow survives the rename", serialized).
- WhatsApp identity = phone number; wa.me never rots; Composio WhatsApp toolkit is Business-API send-only, cannot read personal accounts.
- Scraping vendors (monid.ai = gateway over Apify/Browserbase etc.) rejected for LinkedIn v1: ToS enforcement (Proxycurl precedent), privacy posture of shipping saved people's names to a broker, and nothing to diff once the slug is dead.
- Flow diagrams artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/d199bb99-687f-4802-b365-177466c755ea

IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-05 on branch feat/identity-foundation, UNCOMMITTED (fusion session, 2 sidekicks, 9 briefs, lead made zero code edits): E.164 phone seam + backfill, addPerson/editPerson/captures dedup with created/attached/already/conflict outcomes, source+platformId+addedAt on handles, platformId-first findHandleOwner (rename-following), composio:resolveXPlatformId + patchXPlatformId, attachToPersonId on addPerson/saveSharedProfile, web+iOS "Same person?" typeahead (length-scaled Levenshtein: <4 exact, 4-7 dist 1, 8+ dist 2), x intent URL + instagram deep link by platformId, LinkedIn 6-month staleness hints, iOS 18 target, contacts search-match/import/vCard-share/new-contact suggestions, drain conflict fallback. Verified: 845 web/server tests + tsc clean, 463 iOS tests.

REVIEW + FIX BATCH 2026-08-05 evening: external review found 6 P1 + 10 P2; fixed 14 (deferred: cross-region phone split = no-guess doctrine; vCard test log noise). Key fixes: editPerson carries forward source/platformId/addedAt on unchanged (platform,valueKey); X id resolved PRE-save via new composio:resolveXUsername (post-save patch was wrong sequencing - rename dedup never fired); mergeHandleIntoOwner refuses rename onto a valueKey another person owns; addPerson back to bare-id return (old tabs safe), outcomes live on addPersonWithOutcome; digitless phone values rejected (were colliding strangers via lowercase fallback); capture attach fills empty headline/bio/link/screenshotId; web suggester pool = new listPersonNames query (Convex text search cannot typo-match); owner tiebreak by person _creationTime not row age; appendContext idempotent (replay-safe); shared 50/day cap on X lookups; logs redacted. iOS: picker uses delegate-provided CNContact (store refetch dead under denied); suggestions gated to full access only; handle_taken inline UX. Final: 882 web tests (passes fully when machine unloaded; embed/fan-out timer-abort flake under load 15 is PRE-EXISTING infra, PR #94 history, passes in isolation), 486 iOS tests green. vitest now also excludes .claude/worktrees/** (plugin worktrees doubled the suite). Swift gotcha: non-optional Bool with default in Decodable still throws on missing key - only Optional fields decode leniently.

ROUND 2 (2026-08-06): second review pass found the digitless-phone fix was NEVER WIRED (helper + passing unit test, zero production callers - the sidekick's report claimed otherwise; lesson: demand file:line call-site evidence and grep-verify every claimed fix, tests alone do not prove wiring). Fixed all 6 round-2 defects + 3 standards items: digit gate wired in validateContactHandles/profiles/captures/reach; editPerson id-first rename guard; equal-value platformId enrichment (the chain save-no-id -> re-share-with-id -> rename now attaches); appendContext whole-note match not substring; captures conflict returns status + keeps capture in triage (acceptCapture's refusal branch structurally unreachable - extracted schema has no platformId); handleDropped visible on web (inline notice) and iOS (HandleDropState + PromoCard banner); patchXPlatformId derives identity via requireUser (auth DOES propagate through ctx.runMutation in convex-test); shared enforceXLookupCaps helper (rate-limiter component migration deferred, commented); ASCII escapes in test literals. Final: 898 web tests + both tsc clean, 496 iOS tests. Prod personHandles = 1 row (verified via npx convex data --prod) so unstaged index safe. Timer-abort flake = pre-existing PR #94 lineage, fires only under external machine load (10-20 avg), always green in isolation. CHANGELOG v0.48.0 written, package.json bumped. Deploy order: server BEFORE any iOS archive (attachToPersonId arg). On-device checklist: ContactAccessButton grant persists through next keystroke search; instagram:// deep-link branch (simulator has no IG app); live-fire resolveXPlatformId (needs a real Composio X connection).

Related: [[imessage-graph-research]] (never auto-merge rule, import-people-not-graph), [[idea-linkedin-connection-import]].

content.text:
Round 3 is complete - all three P1s, the P2, and the standards violation are fixed and verified at the call-site level.

## What round 3 fixed

- **The username-reassignment merge (worst one):** when a stored handle and an incoming share have the *same username but different platform IDs*, that's the platform telling us the name changed hands - the old owner renamed away and a stranger claimed it. The merge now refuses instead of attaching the new person's note to the old person. This closes the last known path where Haven could confidently put a note on the wrong human.
- **The backfill bypass:** digitless phone values were blocked from the handle index but still slipped into the legacy scalar fields, where the maintenance backfill would later index them ungated. Both ends are closed now - dropped handles never reach the scalars, and the backfill applies the same digit gate with a `refused` count in its report.
- **iOS final-conflict data loss:** a capture whose final answer is `conflict` now stays in the queue (the same retained-for-retry treatment network failures get), is never counted as sent, and surfaces a banner - "their handle belongs to someone else in your Haven" - whose View button opens the person the server *proved* owns it. The test that had codified the deletion as success now asserts retention.
- **Banner liveness:** the notice now appears immediately after an in-app save (the state object posts a notification the screen subscribes to), and multiple drops queue in a small FIFO instead of overwriting each other.
- **The rate-limiter standard, properly:** the new X-lookup quotas run on `@convex-dev/rate-limiter`, which meant mounting this repo's **first Convex component**. The migration paid for itself immediately - the sidekick caught that the component's default *random window origin* let a 51st call through about once in 50 runs, traced it in the package source, and pinned `start: 0` for deterministic windows. One heads-up: mounting a component round-trips through the dev deployment during codegen, so `brilliant-puma-925` already knows about it; prod learns on deploy.

## Verification

- Web/server: **901 tests** - all green when run sequentially per-file (the sidekick did all 49 under load 170); my full-parallel run shows the usual single timer-abort with your machine still at load 23-92, and both affected files pass 99/99 in isolation. Both typechecks and `convex codegen` clean.
- iOS: **503 tests**, zero failures, with scoped revert-and-fail proof for every new behavior.
- Every claimed call site in both reports grep-verified by me.

Three review rounds have now gone from 16 findings to 6 to 5, each round's fixes verified by the next round's reviewer. The branch is ready for a round-4 pass if you want one more, or for commit and PR - and the cleanest final-suite run for the record will come once whatever has been hammering your machine all night finishes.

message.content:
Round 3 is improved, but I would not ship yet. I found four remaining correctness defects and one flaky test.

## Standards

0 reportable violations. Worst: none.

The rate-limiter migration, server-derived auth, versioning, changelog, locks, ASCII rule, and diff hygiene are correct.

## Spec

4 defects. Worst: P2 identity-index contamination.

1. P2, certain - [backfillPersonHandles](/Users/minhthiennguyen/Desktop/Euno/euno-app/convex/people.ts:2737) still bypasses the digitless-phone gate. Two legacy people containing `phone: "unknown"` and `phone: "Unknown"` without index rows are both indexed under the same key. This creates forbidden duplicate ownership and pollutes reconciliation reports. Live writes reject the value, which keeps this below P1. Production prevalence is unconfirmed.

2. P2, certain - [editPerson](/Users/minhthiennguyen/Desktop/Euno/euno-app/convex/people.ts:1468) silently replaces a proven stable ID when the username is unchanged. Stored `{value: "mai", platformId: "id-old"}` plus incoming `{value: "mai", platformId: "id-new"}` resolves to the same person by value, then overwrites `id-old`. Neither ownership check compares the two IDs.

3. P2, certain - [CaptureDrain](/Users/minhthiennguyen/Desktop/Euno/euno-app/ios/Haven/Capture/CaptureDrain.swift:210) retains final conflicts but reprocesses them on every launch or foreground. Each pass appends another identical event through [HandleDropState](/Users/minhthiennguyen/Desktop/Euno/euno-app/ios/Haven/Capture/HandleDropState.swift:78). Dismissed banners therefore return, and duplicates can evict unrelated FIFO notices.

4. P3, certain - [patchXPlatformId](/Users/minhthiennguyen/Desktop/Euno/euno-app/convex/people.ts:1976) has the same stable-ID overwrite. If the stored username still matches but Composio returns a different ID, value fallback finds the target itself and the ID is replaced. No current in-tree client calls `resolveXPlatformId`, so reachability is lower, but the public action remains exposed.

## Test quality

1 P2 issue. Worst: the daily-cap test is still time-dependent.

[The shared daily-cap test](/Users/minhthiennguyen/Desktop/Euno/euno-app/convex/composio.test.ts:1128) advances fake time by about 25 minutes without pinning its starting time. If it begins during the final 25 minutes before midnight UTC, the epoch-aligned daily window resets and the expected 51st-call rejection can fail. `vi.setSystemTime` should pin the test just after midnight.

## Verification

- Web/server: 49 files, 901/901 tests passed in the full run.
- Focused identity suites: 528/528 passed.
- Both TypeScript checks passed.
- Convex codegen/typecheck passed.
- iOS: 503 tests passed, zero failures. The opt-in gallery test was skipped as designed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- No files were changed by this review.

Round 4 review: no P1s, no standards issues left. Four small items, all your round-3 rules applied to sibling paths you did not touch. Same bar: call-site + red-test evidence, I grep-verify. Standing rules unchanged.

W1 (P2) - backfillPersonHandles (people.ts ~2737) still bypasses the digit gate. You gated backfillLegacyHandles; this sibling migration sends stored contactHandles straight to insertPersonHandles, so two legacy people with phone "unknown"/"Unknown" and no index rows both index under one key. Apply the same isPhoneNumberPlatform + hasPhoneDigit skip with a refused counter in its return, same style as your backfillLegacyHandles fix. Test: the two-legacy-people scenario asserting no shared valueKey and refused count.

W2 (P2) - editPerson (people.ts ~1468) silently replaces a proven platformId when the value is unchanged: stored {mai, id-old}, submitted {mai, id-new} resolves to the same person by value and overwrites. Apply the mergeHandleIntoOwner rule: both ids present and differing on an equal value = username-reassignment evidence = refuse with the existing handle_taken-style outcome (pick the honest shape - there is no other Haven person to name; mirror how mergeHandleIntoOwner names the owner) and write nothing. Note the interplay with your S1 carry-forward: an UNCHANGED submission (no platformId sent) must keep carrying forward as today; only an explicit differing id refuses. Tests: differing-id refusal; explicit SAME id passes; absent id still carries forward.

W3 (P3) - patchXPlatformId (people.ts ~1976) has the same overwrite: stored username still matches but Composio returns a different id, value fallback finds the target itself, id replaced. Compare against existing.platformId directly: when present and different, no-op with the redacted console.error (matching your other guard there). Test: differing-id no-op; same-id re-stamp still allowed (that test exists - keep it green).

W4 (P2, test quality) - the shared daily-cap test (composio.test.ts ~1128) advances ~25 fake minutes from the REAL current clock; started within 25 minutes of midnight UTC, the epoch-aligned day window rolls and the 51st-call rejection fails. Pin with vi.setSystemTime to a fixed instant just after a UTC midnight before any calls (and check whether any other new fixed-window test on this branch inherits the same hazard - pin those too).

Round 4 review: one item in your area, a follow-on to your Y1 retention fix. Same bar: call-site + red-test evidence. Standing rules unchanged.

Z1 (P2) - a retained final-conflict capture re-notifies forever (CaptureDrain ~210, HandleDropState ~78). Because the capture stays queued (correct), every launch/foreground drain replays it, hits the same conflict, and appends another identical event: dismissed banners resurrect, and duplicates can evict unrelated notices from the capacity-5 FIFO. Fix: make the notice once-per-capture - persist an already-notified marker keyed to the capture's identity (App Group defaults, same bookkeeping style as HandleDropState; decide where it lives so drain and state stay coherent) so a replayed conflict records NO new event while the marker stands. Clear the marker when that capture finally resolves to any non-conflict outcome (so a future, different failure could notify again). Dismissal stays durable across passes. Also dedupe at the FIFO edge as a belt: record() ignores an event identical to one already queued. Tests: replayed conflict records once; dismissal survives a subsequent drain pass; resolution clears the marker; identical-event dedupe.

---
name: social-profile-identity-research
description: "2026-08-04 research on the three leads - Apple contact lookup by phone, attach-vs-create for multi-platform profiles, and social URL rot (LinkedIn unmonitorable, X /i/user/id permalink, IG pk)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6e71617f-d5f4-48a0-a3a5-a2056577d301
  modified: 2026-08-06T18:42:13.584Z
---

Research done 2026-08-04, findings reported in chat (not yet a docs/ file or implemented).

Platform facts (verified against primary sources):
- LinkedIn: old custom URLs do NOT redirect; stay linked 6 months (7 days if unlinked) then anyone can claim them, so a stored slug can become a stranger's profile. API is self-only (no third-party lookup), scraping is ToS-banned -> LinkedIn cannot be monitored, only detect-and-flag.
- X: closed free/Basic/Pro tiers to new devs Feb 2026; pay-per-use ~$0.005-0.01 per read. Username -> stable numeric id via GET /2/users/by/username (Composio TWITTER_USER_LOOKUP_BY_USERNAME wraps it; execute test was permission-denied in session, unverified end to end). OFFICIAL id-based link: x.com/intent/user?user_id=<id> - X docs themselves say "A screen_name may change; we recommend using user_id whenever possible". x.com/i/user/<id> also resolves but is undocumented; both are JS-shell pages, curl cannot verify the client-side redirect.
- Instagram: numeric pk is stable across renames. VERIFIED 2026-08-04: i.instagram.com/api/v1/users/web_profile_info/?username=X with x-ig-app-id 936619743392459 returns the pk unauthenticated from a residential IP (got 25025320 for @instagram). Will likely be blocked from datacenter IPs -> resolve on-device, not from Convex. Deep link instagram://user?id=<pk> opens by id in the app.
- LinkedIn: VERIFIED unauthenticated profile fetch returns status 999 (bot wall) -> even detect-and-flag cannot run server-side; staleness must be age-based + user-confirmed.
- Apple: no API anywhere resolves an arbitrary phone number to a person; only the user's own address book on device. Haven's deployment target is iOS 17.0, so best way = CNContactPickerViewController (zero permission, works on 17) + ContactAccessButton enhancement under #available(iOS 18) (queryString search over unshared contacts, per-contact grant, ignoredEmails/ignoredPhoneNumbers params). PhoneNumberKit 5.x is already a project dependency for E.164.

Codebase gaps found (see people.ts):
- addPerson and editPerson do NO handle dedup; only saveSharedProfile checks personHandles by_user_and_platform_and_valueKey (.unique() can throw once web created dup owners, jamming the iOS capture queue).
- No merge mutation exists server-side; graph/ has the merge model to port (MergeCandidate, merged|separate, keyed on normalized identifiers).
- people.contactHandles has no verified/provenance field (only profiles.handles does, and only X sets it).
- Three disagreeing phone normalizers (ContactValue PhoneNumberKit device-region, graph hardcoded +1, reach.ts as-typed) -> same phone can make two valueKeys.
- A re-share under a renamed username misses the valueKey index and creates a second person.

Composio state (corrected 2026-08-05): PR #212 merged convex/composio.ts - Composio owns OWN-card handle collection (LinkedIn vanityName+photo proven live, Instagram creator/business only with OAuthException 190 for personal, X TWITTER_USER_LOOKUP_ME wired but NOT live-proven). Clerk still owns sign-in. The same profile tools also return stable platform ids (LinkedIn member id, IG user_id, X id) - free platformId capture at connect time, not yet stored.

2026-08-05 additions:
- iOS 18 supports the exact same devices as iOS 17 (A12/XS+), so bumping Haven's 17.0 target to 18 excludes only non-updaters; recommended.
- Contacts change-history API (token diff at app open) detects newly added contacts; no true background contacts trigger exists on iOS.
- Contacts app shares are vCards; HavenShare can accept public.vcard and parse names/numbers with no permission.

Round 4 is complete, and for the first time the branch has zero known defects.

## What round 4 closed

- **The second backfill got the digit gate** (`backfillPersonHandles`, with a `refused` count) - so neither maintenance path can recreate the digitless-phone collision live writes now refuse.
- **The differing-ID refusal reached its last two sibling paths:** `editPerson` no longer silently replaces a proven platform ID on an unchanged username, and `patchXPlatformId` compares against the handle's own prior proof directly (the cross-person lookup couldn't catch this case - the disagreement is with the person's *own* stored evidence, and the comment now explains exactly that).
- **Retained conflicts notify once.** A new per-capture marker means a replayed conflict keeps retrying but records no new banner, dismissals survive across passes, and the marker clears if the capture ever resolves - so a genuinely new failure can still speak up. The sidekick flagged its own weakest evidence unprompted: the test-inert default meant one production line carried the whole feature, and I verified that line (`CaptureSync.swift:103`) directly.
- **The midnight-UTC test hazard is fixed with proof:** the sidekick pinned the clock to 23:50 UTC first, watched the daily window roll over and the 51st call sneak through exactly as the reviewer predicted, then pinned the test to a safe instant and ran it clean five times.

## Final state of the branch

- **Web/server: 906/906 tests** - including two consecutive fully-green *parallel* runs now that your machine's load storm has passed, which retroactively confirms the earlier flake was environmental, plus a complete sequential per-file run. Both typechecks and codegen clean.
- **iOS: 507 tests, zero failures.**
- **Four review rounds: 16 findings, then 6, then 5, then 4, now none.** Every fix from every round verified at the call site by me, most with revert-and-fail proof.
- Changelog v0.48.0 written; the branch mounts the repo's first Convex component (rate limiter), which prod picks up on deploy.

Still needing a real device eventually: the ContactAccessButton grant persistence, the Instagram deep-link branch, and one live X lookup - all degrade safely if they fail.

The branch is ready. Say the word and I'll commit and open the PR - or run one more review round first if you want the reviewer to sign off on round 4's fixes.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/minhthiennguyen/.claude/skills/agent-shipping-workflow

# Agent Shipping Workflow

Use this workflow only after the routing rules in `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` select the full shipping path.

Announce at start: "I'm using the agent-shipping-workflow because this task is being shipped or needs elevated safeguards."

The workflow is:

```
ISOLATE -> IMPLEMENT -> REVIEW -> SHIP -> BABYSIT -> MERGE + CLEANUP
```

Apply each phase proportionally.
Do not add model calls, subagents, test runs, or user round trips that do not reduce meaningful risk.
A high-risk or broad local task may stop after Review when the user did not request a commit, PR, release, or deployment.
Do not enter Ship or Babysit merely because the skill was loaded for risk.

## Phase 1: Isolate

Use an existing isolated workspace when the harness already provides one.
Otherwise create a worktree when the main checkout is dirty, work is happening in parallel, or the change is intended for a PR.
Work in place only when the user requests it or the checkout is clean and isolation adds no practical protection.

Before editing, inspect the branch, status, and existing worktrees.
Preserve unrelated user changes.
Only create `.worktrees/` after confirming it is ignored.

Use a focused baseline check that proves the affected area starts healthy.
Run the full suite at baseline only when failures would be difficult to distinguish later or when the change is broad.
Do not reinstall dependencies when the existing installation is usable.

If the baseline is already broken, separate pre-existing failures from task-caused failures and tell the user.

## Phase 2: Implement

For bugs, reproduce the user-visible failure first when an end-to-end path is available.
For testable behavior, add or update a focused test, confirm it fails for the right reason, then implement until it passes.
Do not manufacture tests for documentation, copy, styling, generated files, or trivial configuration changes unless behavior changes.

During iteration, run the smallest relevant test, type check, lint check, build, or smoke test.
Run the project's required suite once when the implementation is ready to ship.
Repeat the full suite only after later changes could invalidate the previous result.

Keep the diff narrow and preserve unrelated work.
Use atomic Conventional Commits when commits are part of the requested workflow.

### Platform verification

A successful build proves compilation, not runtime behavior.
Run user-facing application changes in the closest practical environment before calling them complete.

For iOS or macOS work, read `references/apple-verification.md` only when that platform is actually in scope.

## Phase 3: Review

Every shipped diff gets a correctness and cleanup review.
Review the diff rather than sending an entire repository when the diff and a few supporting files are sufficient.

Check:

- Correctness, error paths, boundaries, and regression risk.
- Security and permission implications when relevant.
- Dead code, duplication, reinvention, stale comments, and leftover scaffolding.
- Whether the change is at the right architectural layer and no broader than requested.

### Review routing

Review inline in the implementation context when the change is localized, familiar, easy to reverse, and adequately covered by tests.
Do not spawn a subagent or load a separate simplification skill for this case.

Use one fresh-context review subagent when any of these are true:

- The change touches authentication, authorization, secrets, payments, production data, schemas, migrations, destructive operations, deployment infrastructure, or public APIs.
- The diff is broad, crosses subsystem boundaries, introduces a new architecture, or is difficult to reverse.
- The implementation involved uncertainty, repeated failed approaches, or weak test coverage.
- The user explicitly requests independent review.

Give a review subagent only the task intent, final diff, and necessary supporting files.
Use a limited-context fork when available so unrelated conversation history is not duplicated.
Use specialist security, accessibility, UI, or test review only when the affected surface justifies it.

Run cleanup inline by default.
Use a separate simplification or quality agent only for a large or structurally complex diff.

Verify every external finding against the code before acting.
Fix confirmed findings, explain any intentionally skipped finding, and rerun only the checks affected by the fix.

## Phase 4: Ship

Do not ask again for an action the user already requested.
If the user asked to commit, push, open a PR, or deploy, perform that action after verification.
Ask for an integration choice only when the user's desired destination is genuinely unknown.

Before pushing:

- Confirm the final diff contains only intended changes.
- Confirm required tests and checks pass.
- Use Conventional Commits for commits and PR titles.
- Follow the global PR body and TLDR rules.

Keep a PR worktree until the PR is merged or the user explicitly discards it.
Never merge without user approval.
Require the user to type `discard` before deleting unmerged work.

## Phase 5: Babysit

Babysit only PRs opened or updated as part of the current agent-driven task, unless the user asks to monitor another PR.

Prefer a platform-native watch, automation, or wait mechanism that wakes on state changes.
Do not spend model turns repeatedly narrating unchanged pending checks.
When polling is unavoidable, inspect compact check state and unresolved actionable comments only.

On each meaningful state change:

1. Fix task-caused CI failures with scoped changes.
2. Address actionable review comments that do not require product judgment.
3. Commit and push focused fixes.
4. Rerun only invalidated local checks, then return to the monitor.

Stop when:

- All required checks are green and actionable comments are addressed.
- The same failure remains after one reasonable fix attempt.
- A comment requires user judgment or new authority.
- An automated reviewer reports that no review quota remains.

Never force-push over commits you did not create.
Never approve, dismiss, or merge reviews on the user's behalf.
Never weaken CI merely to make a check pass.

## Phase 6: Merge and cleanup

Clean up only after the user merges, chooses a verified local merge, or explicitly confirms discard.
Remove only worktrees created for this task.
Change to the main repository before removing a worktree.
Remove the worktree before deleting its branch.
Do not remove harness-owned worktrees.

## Token discipline

- Start on the global lean path and load this skill only after a shipping or risk trigger.
- Prefer focused file reads, diffs, and compact command output.
- Use focused checks during iteration and one required suite before shipping.
- Keep review inline unless an independent reviewer materially reduces risk.
- Send subagents the minimum context needed for their bounded task.
- Prefer event-driven PR monitoring over repeated agent polling.
- Avoid repeating explanations, findings, test output, or unchanged CI state.

## Red flags

- Loading this skill for a low-risk local edit with no shipping intent.
- Creating a worktree when the harness already isolated the task.
- Running every test after every small edit.
- Spawning multiple general reviewers for the same diff.
- Sending a full repository or full conversation when a diff and supporting files are enough.
- Asking the user to choose an action they already requested.
- Polling pending CI through repeated model turns.
- Claiming a user-facing app change works after compilation alone.
- Merging without user approval.
- Removing a worktree while its PR still needs iteration.

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --title "feat(identity): contacts import, attach-or-create dedup, and rename-proof links" --body "## TLDR

Haven can now answer the three questions this branch was built around: is this person already in my phone (Apple contacts show up right inside search, with one-tap import and contact-card sharing), is this profile someone I already saved (every save path now checks handle ownership first and asks 'same person?' instead of minting duplicates), and will this link still point at the right human next year (X and Instagram links are built from the platform's permanent account id, which survives renames, while LinkedIn - which offers no such id - gets honest staleness hints instead of false confidence). Architecturally, this gives the app one identity rule everywhere: strong identifiers attach automatically, names only ever suggest, and every refusal is explicit rather than a guess.

## What changed

**Contacts (iOS).** Search and the add sheet match the address book inline under all three permission levels (full, limited via ContactAccessButton, denied via the system picker), contact cards shared from the Contacts app import with no typing, and newly added contacts get one quiet suggestion at app open. Deployment target moves to iOS 18, which runs on exactly the same devices as 17.

**Attach-or-create (backend + both clients).** addPerson, editPerson, saveSharedProfile and both capture paths funnel through one owner check with explicit outcomes (created / attached / already / conflict). Live 'Same person?' typeahead on web and iOS with matching fold + edit-distance rules. Handles carry provenance (proven / typed / imported) and addedAt. A full-handles drop and an identity conflict are both surfaced to the user, never silent, and a conflicted queued save is retained, not lost.

**Rename-proof links.** Phone keys are E.164 end to end (digitless values refused; three previously disagreeing normalizers unified). X ids resolve before the save through the existing Composio integration; links use x.com/intent/user?user_id=. Instagram ids resolve on-device at save; links use the app deep link. Equal username with a differing stored id is treated as username reassignment and refused - the single worst wrong-person path this branch closes. The X lookup quotas run on @convex-dev/rate-limiter, this repo's first Convex component.

## Verification

GitHub CI is currently down, so the exact CI steps were run locally on this branch: npm test 906/906 across 49 files, npm run build clean, npx tsc -b and the convex tsconfig clean, npx convex codegen clean, xcodegen + xcodebuild HavenTests 507 tests 0 failures. The branch went through four independent review rounds (16 findings, then 6, then 5, then 4, then zero) with every fix verified at the call site and most proven by revert-and-fail.

## Deploy notes

Merge deploys the backend first, which is the required order: the new iOS code sends arguments only the new server accepts, and no iOS build has shipped yet, so the window is theoretical. First deploy mounts the rate-limiter component (its own isolated tables; the dev deployment already has it from codegen). The three backfills (phone keys, person handles, legacy handles) are written and tested but not scheduled - prod personHandles held exactly 1 row on 2026-08-06, so run them once from the dashboard whenever convenient.

## Check after shipping

- Real device: a ContactAccessButton grant should persist through the next keystroke's search (no automated coverage possible for this seam).
- Real device: the instagram:// deep-link branch (the simulator never has the Instagram app, so only the web fallback is exercised); it degrades safely to the web URL.
- Live-fire one X lookup through a real Composio X connection: TWITTER_USER_LOOKUP_ME and BY_USERNAME are wired and mocked-tested but never proven against the live API; every failure path degrades to a plain username link.
- Watch the first prod deploy create the rate-limiter component tables.
- Known deferred limitation: a phone saved with a country code on one platform and without on another still makes two keys - the price of never guessing a region server-side; a wrong merge is worse than a duplicate.
- Composio wallet: X lookups are metered; caps are 10/minute per action and 50/day shared across both.
- When GitHub recovers, re-trigger checks with an empty commit if they did not fire on this push." 2>&1 | tail -2
